issues.description: The custom `ManuallyDrop<T>` stores its payload as an ordinary `T`, so Rust's automatic field drop glue still destroys `T` when the wrapper is dropped instead of preserving manual-drop semantics.
issues.rationale: At the selected human-review commit, the wrapper is named `ManuallyDrop` and carries a ghost obligation, but its executable field is still `value: T`. Rust therefore generates ordinary field-destruction behavior for the payload when the wrapper goes out of scope; the ghost obligation has no effect on executable drop glue. Human reviewer hiroki-chen identifies this concrete mismatch, the author explicitly agrees it is a source-code flaw, and the subsequent fix commit replaces the field with `core::mem::ManuallyDrop<T>`, wraps construction with `ManuallyDrop::new`, and extracts with `ManuallyDrop::into_inner`.

The same historical revision constructs the wrapper with `Self { value: t }` at line 92. Fix commit 757d75d9ef1b8528b697b830277d441ea614d374 changes line 76 to `value: core::mem::ManuallyDrop<T>`, construction to `core::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(t)`, and extraction to `std::mem::ManuallyDrop::<T>::into_inner(slot.value)`.
